All Native Americans from Alaska all the way to Patagonia came from central Asia. They crossed a land bridge between eastern Russia and Alaska and colonized/settled all over North, Central, South America and the Caribbean.

The new humans kicked off what is known as the Pleistocene Mass Extinction event, which was the first mass extinction event attributed to homo sapiens. This mass extinction event saw the death of most American megafauna. Remind the natives of this every time they pretend as if they have some deeper connection to the environment.
Am rusty on the megafauna extinction. Care to refresh my memory?

Sure! From what I can recall starting around ~20,000 - 14,000 years ago the first homo sapiens began arriving in North America. They followed game herds across a land bridge that connected what is now eastern Russia with what is now Alaska across what we call the Bearing Strait.

At this time a large part of North America was covered by a massive glacier. The wildlife in North America was at least as diverse as modern day Africa, probably more so. This was the time of Woolly Mammoths, Mastodons, Short Faced Bears, American Lions, American Camels, Dire Wolves, Giant Ground Sloths, Megatherium, Sabre Tooth Cats, and many others. These are collectively known as the Pleistocene Megafauna.

As the ice age ended and the massive glacier receded, this allowed the first homo sapiens in North America to expand across the continent. The animals who had lived here since time immortal, had survived and adapted through many ice ages and warmer periods. Although the warming climate was responsible for changing weather and climate, the true X factor that lead to the demise of such a wide variety of so many successful animal species was a new innovative hunter that would hunt in groups, fashion tools like spears and spear heads out of flint, and could also communicate, plan, and co ordinate attacks to take down much larger game species.

The Megafauna of the Americas had never dealt with a predator as unique and ingenious as the homo sapiens. Its is believed they would target primarily Woolly Mammoths and Mastodons as coordinated hunter groups. They would follow the herds, pick out the weakest or most vulnerable member of the pack, they could ambush them, hurling spears and causing wounds to the animals. The herds would get frightened and stampede and leave the weaker members of the herd to be attacked by the homo sapiens and bleed out over hours or even days. There is evidence that the homo sapiens would sometimes even channel the herds into valleys next to cliffs and push large rocks onto the animals, breaking their bones and rendering them immobile.

The homo sapiens populations exploded, they had a ready source of food, very high in protein, they refined their hunting techniques, and were able to feed increasing population groups, which meant more hunters, expanding to new territory as they were primarily nomadic at that time.

Because the homo sapiens were such a new predator in the land, the original inhabitants could not evolve quickly enough to defend against this new predator. The decimation of the populations by hunting combined with the changing environmental factors lead to the death of key animal species for the ecosystem. Likely the Woolly Mammoths were hunted to such an extent that their population could not recover and they went extinct. This removed a key species from the ecosystem which would have effected all of the other animals.

With the introduction of homo sapiens, they marginalized other predators in the land, like the Sabre Toothed Cats, Cave Bears and Dire Wolves, causing populations of those predators to decrease. As the predators numbers decreased, it would have lead to temporary population explosions of prey species, like the ancient American Horses. These herd species would clear out the healthy vegetation in an area, which would prevent new vegetation from growing and would end up causing mass die offs of these herd species due to starvation, leaving the rest of the weakened herd to be picked off by predators. This is similar to what happens in modern times, at places like Yellowstone park, where humans killed off all the wolves and the deer and elk populations exploded. They ate through and destroyed the underbrush to such an extent that the herds starved to death en mass. Humans had to reintroduce wolves to the park to help control the population of the prey species.

So to sum up: The ancestors of what we call "Native Americans" arrived in the Americas during the end of the last ice age. They were a new predator species in the land, with indigenous animal species that had never encountered humans before, and had no inherent fear of man. These first humans in North America hunted key prey species to an extent these species numbers got reduced enough that the hunting, combined with the environmental changes during the warming period at the end of the ice age, cause these species to go extinct. This caused a ripple effect through the food chain in the ecosystem and led to massive die offs of numerous Megafauna animal species over 100lbs.
